name: cross-dataset flow detector, version 2, CIC-IDS2017 to CSE-CIC-IDS2018
registered: 2026-11-20, before any version 2 result was read
relation_to_version_1: Version 1 (experiment-b/cic-flow, evidence docs/evidence/MEASURED_CROSS_DATASET_FLOW_DETECTOR_2026_11_19.md) failed its 1% benign alert budget on CSE-CIC-IDS2018 (30.85%). Version 1 read every 2018 label once. Version 2 changes the design in response to that result, so its 2018 measurement is a second measurement on the same data, not an untouched held-out test. The version 1 result stays on record unchanged.
changes_from_version_1: thresholds and the anomaly model are set on the protected network's own traffic: the first 2018 day, all flows, labels not read, as a deployment's first day would be
context computed in timestamp order; out-of-order rows counted and reported
feature and scoring code hashed into the freeze and checked before scoring
2017 development reported by leave-one-day-out instead of a random row split

development.dataset: CIC-IDS2017, improved version by Engelen, Rimmer and Joosen (CNS 2022), regenerated with the fixed CICFlowMeter

test.dataset: CSE-CIC-IDS2018, improved version by the same authors, same fixed CICFlowMeter

labels: BENIGN and every label containing 'Attempted' are benign (the dataset authors' recommendation for flows without attack behaviour). Every other label is an attack. Families come from features_v2.FAMILY_PATTERNS; a test label matching none is reported as 'unmapped'.
inputs: features_v2.build: signed-log flow statistics (all non-identifier numeric columns), protocol one-hot, destination-service bucket, two per-destination 60-second context counts computed in timestamp order. Never inputs: id, Flow ID, IP addresses, ports, timestamp, label.

models.supervised: sklearn HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=200, learning_rate=0.1, max_leaf_nodes=31, class_weight='balanced', early_stopping=False, random_state=20261120), fit on every CIC-IDS2017 row, attack versus benign. Frozen before any 2018 flow is read by v2 code.
models.anomaly: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=200, max_samples=1024, random_state=20261120), fit at calibration on the first 200,000 calibration-day flows in file order with split_bucket 0-4; score = -score_samples
models.alert: supervised attack probability > t_s OR anomaly score > t_a

calibration.why_this_day: first day in time order; chosen by that rule, not by version 1 per-day results
calibration.rows_for_thresholds: split_bucket 5-9 of the calibration day, all flows, labels not read
calibration.budget: t_s and t_a each at 0.5% of those flows (features_v2.benign_threshold), so at most 1% of calibration-day flows alert
calibration.excluded_from_test: every flow of the calibration day

development_reporting: for each 2017 day with attacks (tuesday to friday): supervised refit without that day; anomaly model and thresholds set on that day exactly as the calibration step does (fit on buckets 0-2, first 200,000; thresholds on buckets 3-5, labels not read); TP, FP, FN, TN on buckets 6-9, per family. Reported as they come out; nothing above changes because of them.
freeze: supervised model bytes SHA-256; SHA-256 of features_v2.py, train_dev_v2.py, score_test_v2.py and this file; both source pins. The test stage refuses to run on any mismatch.
test_reporting: the nine non-calibration 2018 days, every flow, once: TP, FP, FN, TN, detection rate and benign alert rate with Wilson 95% intervals, precision, per family, per day, which part fired, out-of-order rows per day. Pass condition, stated in advance: benign alert rate at most 1% pooled and on every day.
not_claimed: Performance on networks other than these two lab captures; attack types absent from both; real-time operation; that the 2018 data is unseen (see relation_to_version_1).
